mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 4% over the next month reduces the present value of future equity cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over a 20-day horizon.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by 0.25% in the following month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive despite FEDFUNDS increase, or IC > 0.05 over the horizon.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) coinciding with a decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strengthening labor market, which elevates consumer confidence and equity valuations, driving positive 60-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >2% while UNRATE falls by >0.2% in the next month
failure_condition: IC < 0.0 over 60-day window or no correlation between PAYEMS/UNRATE movement and SPX returns.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in housing starts (HOUST) above 1,200K for three consecutive months indicates accelerating domestic demand, which anticipates a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return as market pricing in future economic expansion.
failure_condition: 20-day returns negative despite three consecutive months of HOUST > 1200K.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% in a month suggests supply-side weakness, lowering growth expectations and producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by >2% in the following month
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns positive or IC > 0.1 over the horizon.

mechanism_narrative: When the monthly inflation rate (CPIAUCSL) exceeds 2.5% for two consecutive months, the market anticipates the Fed will maintain higher rates, depressing equity valuations and yielding negative 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL rises above 2.5% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day returns positive despite CPIAUCSL > 2.5% for two months.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4.5% triggers a labor market tightening that raises wage growth expectations, pushing 60-day S&P 500 forward returns to the positive.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls below 4.5% in the next month

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent increases in retail sales (PAYEMS) and consumer confidence (not available in evidence - so skip this proxy) cannot be used; instead, a rise in industrial production (INDPRO) above 100 (monthly) for two months signals demand recovery, producing positive 20-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: 20-day returns flat or negative during two months of INDPRO > 100.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in monthly retail sales (PAYEMS) of 5% or more indicates weakening demand, which the market interprets as a supply-side constraint, resulting in negative 60-day S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: 60-day returns positive despite continuous PAYEMS decline.
